routes.name: Permiso especial de permanencia por contrato

note: Honduras, read on 2026-10-30 in the Ley de Migración y Extranjería (Decree 208-2003) as published in La Gaceta of 3 March 2004 (No. 30,331), in the scan FAO's FAOLEX database holds (the Instituto Nacional de Migración's own copy of the law answered with a 522 timeout from its host on 2026-10-30, and its Extranjería page lists services without terms); later amendments and the regulation weren't read, so the 2004 text is what is written. Foreigners may be residents as rentistas, pensionados or inversionistas, the family of these, the spouse of a Honduran by birth, the parents of Honduran children, and, after five years as lawful residents or on a special stay permit, those acquiring the right to settle (art. 21); residence is applied for to the Secretaría de Gobernación y Justicia if the foreigner is in Honduras, or to a Honduran consul if abroad (art. 22: 'either' on the residence routes). Foreigners contracted by persons or institutions established in Honduras may take a special stay permit by contract (art. 40), checked with the Labour Ministry; special stay permits run up to five years (a ceiling, so no term is written), and the law doesn't say where they are applied for. A resident with a job or a job offer must also get the Labour Ministry's work card (art. 15) and no foreigner may carry on activities other than those expressly authorised (art. 57); the law doesn't say whether a contract permit ties its holder to the employer, so what work each allows isn't written. A resident becomes a residente inmigrado (permanent) after five consecutive years, having renewed the resident's card or special permit every year (art. 37: 5 written on every route, and renewable on the residence routes). No fees or decision times are in the law, nor whether the years count toward naturalisation; non-resident artists may be authorised to work by the Secretaría (art. 16), which is the work engine's.
